scenes.heading: Pronumerals on both sides
scenes.sub: When x turns up on the left AND the right
scenes.say: Five x plus three equals two x plus eighteen. Now x is on both sides! Don't worry. One extra step gets it back to an equation you already know how to solve.
scenes.caption: 5x + 3 = 2x + 18. Now x is on both sides! Don't worry. One extra step gets it back to an equation you already know how to solve.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Scales: 5 bags + 3 marbles balance 2 bags + 18 marbles
scenes.science: Take 2 bags off each pan: 3x + 3 = 18, so each bag holds 5
scenes.breaks: you can't put a negative number of bags on a pan, but equations can have terms like −2x.
scenes.say: Picture old scales. Five bags of marbles and three loose marbles balance two bags and eighteen loose marbles. Take two bags off each pan and it still balances. Then three bags and three marbles equal eighteen, so each bag holds five marbles.

scenes.heading: Balance the scales
scenes.say: Here are the scales. Five bags and three marbles on the left, two bags and eighteen marbles on the right. Take two bags off each side: still balanced. Take three marbles off each side. Now three bags balance fifteen marbles, so each bag holds five.
scenes.caption: Five bags and 3 marbles on the left, 2 bags and 18 marbles on the right. Take 2 bags off each side: still balanced. Take 3 marbles off each side. Now 3 bags balance 15 marbles, so each bag holds 5.

scenes.heading: The method
steps: Move the numbers to the other side
scenes.say: Here's the method. Expand any brackets. Subtract the smaller x-term from both sides. Then deal with the numbers, divide by the coefficient, and check by working out each side separately.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Solve 7x − 4 = 3x + 16.
scenes.say: Solve seven x minus four equals three x plus sixteen. Subtract three x from both sides: four x minus four equals sixteen. Add four: four x equals twenty. Divide by four: x equals five. Check: both sides give thirty-one.
scenes.caption: Solve 7x − 4 = 3x + 16. Subtract 3x from both sides: 4x − 4 = 16. Add 4: 4x = 20. Divide by 4: x = 5. Check: both sides give 31.

scenes.heading: A negative x-term
scenes.question: Solve 3 − 2x = x + 15.
scenes.say: Solve three minus two x equals x plus fifteen. To get rid of negative two x, add two x to both sides: three equals three x plus fifteen. Subtract fifteen: negative twelve equals three x. So x equals negative four.
scenes.caption: Solve 3 − 2x = x + 15. To get rid of −2x, add 2x to both sides: 3 = 3x + 15. Subtract 15: −12 = 3x. So x = −4.

scenes.heading: Which gym?
scenes.question: Gym A: $60 + $5 a visit. Gym B: $15 a visit. When do they cost the same?
scenes.say: Gym A charges sixty dollars to join plus five dollars a visit. Gym B charges fifteen dollars a visit. Sixty plus five v equals fifteen v. Subtract five v: sixty equals ten v. So v equals six. They cost the same, ninety dollars, after six visits.
scenes.caption: Gym A charges $60 to join plus $5 a visit. Gym B charges $15 a visit. 60 + 5v = 15v. Subtract 5v: 60 = 10v. So v = 6. They cost the same, $90, after 6 visits.

points: Letters to one side, numbers to the other
scenes.say: Quick recap. Letters to one side, numbers to the other. Remove the smaller x-term, expand brackets first, and check that both sides match. Now try the practice questions!
